findings.title: Convergence assertion in 5.2 is too weak to prove the success criterion
findings.description:
The criterion says the herd's mean heading "converges toward the leaders' initial heading". Task 5.2 only asserts that the mean heading has a positive x-component. With 45 random-velocity agents, a positive x-component can occur with no leadership effect at all, so the test can pass without the forces doing anything and can also be seed-sensitive. The control comparison that makes the result meaningful is only in 5.3, and 5.3 uses an "or" assertion (lower variance OR stronger eastward bias, lines 160-161). That "or" lets either metric pass trivially.

Fix: merge 5.2 and 5.3 into one test run against the flocking-only control. Assert one pre-chosen metric, for example that the herding mean eastward component exceeds the control's by a stated margin.

findings.title: Redundant tasks: 5.1 overlaps 5.2, and Section 6 repeats earlier verifications
findings.description:
- **5.1:** 5.2 already runs all five forces through `tick()`. 5.1 adds only a "runs without error" check, and its step "confirm forces interact correctly" (line 144) has no assertion.
- **6.2:** it repeats the `isinstance` checks already in 3.1, 3.2, 4.1 and 4.2.
- **6.1:** it repeats the full-suite runs at the end of 1.2 and 2.2.

Cut 5.1 (or fold it into the merged 5.2/5.3 test) and drop 6.2. Keep 6.1 as the final gate, merged into the last commit task.

findings.title: Commit steps are checkbox tasks, and 6.3 may be a bookkeeping-only commit
findings.description: Project convention is plain `**Commit**:` marker lines, never checkboxes. Here every commit is a numbered, checked-off task (1.3, 2.3, 3.3, 4.3, 5.4, 6.3). Replace them with plain `**Commit**:` lines at the same working, tested points. 6.3 says "git add any remaining changes" with a `docs:` message. If everything is already committed, that commit would only check boxes or add notes, which the project forbids. Drop 6.3 and put the final commit marker after the last test task.

findings.title: Epsilon is specified twice as an inline example literal
findings.description: Tasks 3.1 and 4.1 each say "epsilon (e.g. 1e-10)". Project rules forbid scattered magic values and duplicated constants. A junior implementer will likely hard-code `1e-10` in both forces. Add a step in 3.1 to define one named module-level constant in `herding.py`, and have 4.1 reference it.

findings.title: "Vectorized, no nested Python loops" has no explicit task step
findings.description: The technical requirement says both forces are vectorized within each agent's neighborhood. Task 4.1 writes the weighted average as `sum(velocity[i] * leadership[i]) / sum(leadership)`, which a junior could implement as an inner Python loop. Add a step stating that the per-neighbor weighted average uses NumPy array operations (indexing plus a weighted sum) inside a single per-agent loop.

findings.title: Profile lookup per agent is not described
findings.description: Tasks 3.1 and 4.1 use `profile.momentum_weight` and `profile.leadership_weight` but never say how to get an agent's profile from `state.profile_indices` and `profiles`. Point to the equivalent lookup in `src/migratory/engine/flocking.py` so the implementer follows the same pattern.

findings.title: Test count in MomentumForce tests is slightly generous
findings.description: The known case, the direction test and the magnitude-scaling test (lines 96-98) overlap heavily for a one-line formula. This is acceptable, but the direction and scaling tests could be a single parametrized test.
